topic.title: Passing Arguments by Values
topic.description: How arguments are passed to methods

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s break down how Java handles arguments when you pass them to methods. It’s simpler than you think!

• How Java passes values (not variables) to methods
• Why changing a parameter inside a method doesn’t affect the original value
• Common mistakes and how to avoid them

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you’re photocopying a document. The original stays safe, but you can scribble all over the copy. That’s how Java passes arguments!

When you pass a variable to a method, Java creates a *copy* of its value. The method works with this copy, leaving the original untouched.

• **Primitive types** (like `int`, `double`) are passed *by value* – a full copy is made
• **Objects** are passed *by reference value* – the copy points to the same object (but the reference itself is copied!)
• Changing the copy inside the method won’t affect the original variable

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Java passes all arguments by value: a copy of the value is passed to the method
Changing a parameter inside a method does not affect the original argument variable
For primitive types, the value itself is copied
For object types, the reference value is copied (both point to the same object)
Understanding pass-by-value is essential for predicting method behavior

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Java passes arguments *by value* – always a copy, never the original. Changing a parameter inside a method won’t affect the original variable. Practice writing methods that return modified values instead of trying to change parameters.

questions.question: In Java, how are primitive type arguments passed to methods?
questions.explanation: Java passes primitive type arguments by value, meaning a copy of the value is passed to the method. Changes to the parameter inside the method do not affect the original variable.

questions.question: If you change a parameter's value inside a method, does the original argument change?
options: No, for primitive types the original is unchanged
Only if the parameter is final
questions.explanation: For primitive types, changes to a parameter inside a method do not affect the original argument because Java passes a copy of the value.
